review_during_edit.followup_review: Re-read the added AppendFacts capacity and selected reader WrittenBank validation, plus the existing all-append terminal-success latch before first take. The final source identities above, rather than the initial identities, bind the observations below.

checked.topic: Typed external write and ordinary DAG scheduling
checked.observation: PagedAppend is an explicit external side effect with exact plain F16/BF16 row input and no tensor output. Descriptor geometry is checked against its paged schema/role/row count. The selected provider declares preserves_effects and uses the original shared Queue sequence. This is not a pure tensor operation or a separate executor. Encoded storage and delegated native readers are not silently treated as this reference path.

checked.topic: Actual selected artifacts and direct write-before-read proof
checked.observation: The writer proof is obtained from the actual selected singleton append slot, with NodeId, plan step, prepared VTable and prepared object identity. Core independently checks generation/node-step mapping, the original Graph external-effect trait, artifact identity and shared Queue mode. Every qualified reader must be a selected shared Queue singleton after the writer and have an explicit original Graph dependency on that writer. The common projection validates the real physical input port and rejects any extra unqualified consumer, capacity output or physical alias descendant. A caller-supplied ordinal or provider-family identity alone does not authorize writing/reading pages.

checked.topic: Exact page authority; no whole-bank mutable permission
checked.observation: Each dirty writer is checked as the original arena page reservation, matching physical range, root identity, generation, current acquired state and initialized prefix. Repeated roots/pages and mixed ready/writable identities are rejected. The cache capacity remains a ConstTensorView for addressing; begin_submission registers only the original exact page WriteLeases plus old exact ReadLeases in the existing LeaseUseBatch/permissions. It does not manufacture an exclusive whole-bank lease. The added selected reader WrittenBank guard checks the owned layout, description and exact resource/native-handle/offset/size before enqueueing attention.

checked.topic: Complete COW prefix and appended-row initialization
checked.observation: Each request must extend the validated old history by exactly its packed query rows. Untouched prefix pages must retain their physical IDs and exact old guards. A partially retained page must use a distinct dirty page: its entire inherited initialized prefix is copied first, then the exact newly produced row range, with the correct per-request source offset. Dirty pages cannot be shared between requests, unused, repeated or already initialized. Successful publication exposes only the required initialized row prefix; the unused physical tail is not made readable by this path. Layout validation bounds logical rows by the signed-32-bit schema capacity, and row geometry is validated before size-based offsets are computed.

checked.topic: Accepted-prefix lifetime and explicit failure recovery
checked.observation: Each actual transfer returns its original accepted flag; a later error preserves an already accepted prefix in the ordinary Queue/completion path. The append slot retains its arena, previous frame, dirty writers and exact views through retirement. The original LeaseUseBatch keeps native uses alive and poisons write generations on a failed terminal; such generations are never ready. Existing explicit recovery is take_append after actual retirement, page.lease().reset(), then page.discard(); discard reclaims only after the original pool proves all actual uses/permissions have retired and creates a fresh generation with initialized_rows=0.
checked.limitation: Dropping an owner while its original failed WriteLease remains valid can park that poisoned generation in the arena. This review does not claim automatic failed-page recycling; callers must follow the existing explicit recovery contract.

checked.topic: Whole-Graph publication, take, reset and replay invalidation
checked.observation: Only an actually successful idle whole-Graph terminal with no retained Graph results/observations authorizes ready(). Before the first take invalidates output readiness, take latches that same terminal success for all bound append transactions, enabling independent K/V take without publishing early. take is nonblocking and refuses pending work. It invalidates the actual writer and reader recordings, removes exact permission bindings and unbinds the raw cache carrier before returning original page reservations. Batch reset refuses an untaken append transaction, and a previously successful transaction cannot be rebound as fresh. Ready-frame allocation failure can retry with already-published exact page leases retained.

checked.topic: Queue source bridge and reservation precede physical allocation
checked.observation: The append adapter retains the same actual ExecutionSource/Context and selected resource; shared Queue source validation requires exact owner/interface and no fabricated numerical provider index. TransferAccess enqueues byte copies through the original backend Queue vtable and normal Graph submit path. PagedArena uses the original LeasePool with backing plus sentinel capacity checked first. prepare_lease_domain reserves the ResourceBudget charge before Buffer::create; owner/member lifetimes retain it until the backing and original native-use references are released. No model-ID allowlist or per-model routing policy is introduced.

resolved_question.initial_concern: A failed original writer remains valid/poisoned and direct drop parks it, so automatic reacquisition is not proven.
resolved_question.resolution: Existing nonconst PagedPageWriter::lease() explicitly allows reset; discard() then uses actual lease-pool retirement to recover the original physical page with a fresh generation. The implementation owner confirmed this intended contract and the new source test spells out reset/discard. No additional product edit was requested.

conclusion.selected_first_delivery: Real Qwen whole-state snapshot and explicit prefix fork, using existing Graph execution and current strict COW append; one engine-level head commit after all 12 KV frames and 36 conv/GDN outputs are ready.
conclusion.do_not_claim: This is not yet exclusive-tail append, arbitrary-token prefix slicing, MTP accepted-prefix commit, merged multi-request execution, or all-platform full-model validation.
conclusion.critical_preintegration_fix: PagedAppend.rows is fixed in a custom descriptor, whereas current Qwen compiles several T children from one symbolic Graph. Derive row count from the exact input description in cold prepare rather than duplicating a fixed T in the logical operation.

established_facts.fact: Qwen has 24 layers: six attention layers with BF16 dense K/V and eighteen linear layers with BF16 [1,3,6144] conv history and F32 [1,16,128,128] recurrent state. Every Session currently owns dense K/V plus two ping-pong state sets.

The present mathematical Graph already reads old conv/GDN state and produces complete next_history/next_recurrent as distinct published outputs. A pre-copy/clone of these states is not needed merely to preserve the old snapshot; bind a fresh output block and share the old input read lease.

Current six attention layers Scatter into the same bound dense K/V banks before RaggedAttention. Failure invalidates the Session. length and parity advance after GPU completion but before the host next_id read, so this is not a complete immutable snapshot transaction.

The new bridge owns exact dirty pages, copies only needed old-tail prefix/new rows on the original QueueSequence, and requires actual whole-Graph success before ready(). It currently requires fresh targets, a distinct COW tail page, singleton selected writer and reader regions, and direct original Graph control edges.
StateStore supports a fixed member schema of resource leases and copied host metadata; StateHead only atomically publishes a StateVersion. It does not own a variable vector of PagedArenaRead frames.

SessionCache is serialized count/fixed-reported-byte metadata. Its contract explicitly excludes shared backing deduplication and asynchronous page accounting. Current dense-session admission cannot silently be reused as a physical shared-page byte ledger.

minimal_shape.model_owner: Retain immutable weights, one logical Graph/finite selected family, existing Context/Queue, per-layer/role shared physical arenas, bounded recurrent output LeasePools, and their real ResourceBudget reservations. Sessions hold exact frames/readers; do not allocate a complete physical arena per prefix/session.
minimal_shape.whole_snapshot: An engine-private immutable aggregate: six exact key frames, six exact value frames, the 36 conv/GDN read resources (optionally one existing StateVersion over those fixed entries), and committed token/position metadata for the actual current model. Retain the actual model/resource owners. One aggregate head is the publication unit.
minimal_shape.state_version_boundary: Use StateVersion only if useful for the fixed 36 recurrent/history resources; variable page lists remain in PagedArenaRead. Do not encode all possible physical page IDs as fixed StateSchema entries, put owning C++ handles into opaque metadata bytes, or publish a separate StateHead and KV head in two operations.
minimal_shape.head_and_pin: Reuse the current externally serialized Session pin/turn boundary and a single private aggregate head/generation. A brief existing session mutex would suffice if later necessary; no new lock-free directory or scheduler is required. parity becomes only an invocation-slot choice and is not authoritative model position/state.
minimal_shape.prefix: First provide an explicit fork/restore at an evaluated boundary. Share its immutable whole aggregate and append distinct continuations. A KV prefix alone cannot reconstruct conv/GDN state at an arbitrary earlier token. Prefix lookup later must match actual model/adapter, exact token sequence, absolute-position and numerical semantics; provider family names do not confer identity.
minimal_shape.retention: Keep only selected latest heads and explicitly retained prefixes/branches, not a StateVersion at every historical token. Distinct prefix snapshots keep recurrent buffers alive; later pool reuse waits for their final readers/native use.

transaction_sequence.action: Before admission reserve required new dirty pages and complete conv/GDN output blocks under real physical budgets; construct bounded candidate metadata. Bind immutable old state, one pair of append nodes per attention layer, exact target layouts, and fresh state outputs into the same original Invocation. Explicitly order both K/V append nodes before that layer attention; retain existing conservative external-effect ordering.

Call existing batch prepare, then bind_append, then prepare_replay, then one Graph submit. No engine per-layer copy submissions, second executor, or fake writable whole-arena view. Keep the old aggregate head and all original pending owners charged until actual outcome/retirement is known.

After actual successful completion, export all published conv/GDN storage leases and any required host next_id first. Drop every GraphOutput result guard. This ordering matters: first take_append invalidates whole-Graph output readiness, and active result guards prevent its retired gate.

Take all original append owners and obtain all exact ready K/V frames; current success latch covers all append owners before the first take releases a projection. Finalize any fixed-state StateDraft and create the complete candidate. A ready per-layer frame is still private; never replace layer heads incrementally.

Only after every fallible candidate/output operation succeeds, compare the original head/generation and replace the single aggregate head. Advance visible length/absolute positions with that same commit. An unsuccessful commit leaves the previous whole snapshot unchanged; retire/drop the unpublished candidate normally.

exclusive_in_place_append.fact: PagedArena.acquire(ReadLease&) already preserves initialized bytes/generation when actual reader/native exclusivity succeeds, but current PagedAppendPages.create retains the previous frame, forbids same physical tail, and rejects initialized_rows>0.
exclusive_in_place_append.not_enough_to_loosen_checks: Keeping the previous frame pins its old ready page. Consuming/dropping the sole old tail reader can permit exclusivity, but current full-page WriteLease admission poisons the whole block on an accepted Graph error. reset()+discard() then gives a new uninitialized generation, not the old committed tail.
exclusive_in_place_append.transactional_constraint: With current failure-granularity contract one cannot promise both unchanged old-head rollback and zero-copy exclusive reuse of that same tail merely from acquire(). This remains true even if the native copy intended to touch only the suffix: core tracks failure at whole LeaseBlock granularity.
exclusive_in_place_append.first_delivery: Keep true COW for partial tails in the complete-snapshot first delivery, including single-user sessions. State its cost and do not treat this as the final performance shape.
next_narrow_choices: A consumed exclusive-append mode may explicitly invalidate/recompute the session after accepted failure; it must not claim that the prior snapshot remains usable.

For strong rollback, a later precise suffix-write contract must actually preserve and re-authorize the committed prefix after real retirement, or retain a recoverable tail backup. This needs a real range/generation/failure design; discard currently deliberately promises no preserved initialized bytes.
exclusive_in_place_append.ownership_requirement: A future exclusive overload must consume/extract the unique old frame authority without the transaction retaining a duplicate ready tail guard; failed acquisition preserves original authority and can fall back to COW. Do not publicly expose raw arena capacity to accomplish it.

failure_and_recovery.one_owner: Introduce one small engine-private step transaction/abort helper for all 12 append owners and state-output bindings. It tracks locally reserved, bound, recovered and published ownership; no generic new transaction framework.
failure_and_recovery.abort_contract: On prepare/replay/zero-command rejection, accepted error, cancellation or closure, first preserve the real accepted prefix and prove native retirement/observer release. Then take every original append owner, reset each failed page lease and discard explicitly; retain ownership and charge if discard reports Unavailable. Cancel any fixed-state draft and retain the old aggregate head.
failure_and_recovery.poison_drop: Do not rely on PagedPageWriter destructor as automatic failed-page recovery. A still-valid failed writer can park in the arena; the existing explicit reset/discard protocol must be centralized so exceptions do not strand it.
failure_and_recovery.state_outputs: Bind new recurrent/history outputs using owned WriteLease, never a raw mutable view of a retained snapshot. Current private take_write rejects failed Graph phase; let the failed original Invocation retire/destroy its owned state output bindings before their pool ranges can be reused. If reusable failure recovery is needed, add only the exact observed missing extraction seam, not a forced reset of a failed Invocation.
failure_and_recovery.no_hidden_wait: Normal transaction finalization observes the already-completed work; retryable abort ownership remains attached to its actual Session until safe reclamation. Do not use drain() as a normal reusable-success reset because it closes admission.

fusion_proof_boundary.current_restriction: bind_append discovers only the private batch region_table readers; core requires node_count==1 and reads that singleton logical node for the direct writer dependency. Writer discovery also requires exactly one append node in its selected artifact. Thus a legitimate attention+epilogue fused region, or append+attention fused region, currently declines.
fusion_proof_boundary.first_delivery: Keep the current strict singleton proof for a first real Qwen paged route. If current selected paged attention is unsupported, fail/decline visibly; do not disable fusion globally or quietly route back to whole dense-bank writes.
fusion_proof_boundary.first_generalization_if_actual_fused_rea: Carry the actual logical reader NodeId alongside the exact selected region/prepared/physical input-port proof. Verify its original Graph membership and node_steps mapping, the explicit dependency from that logical attention node to the original append, and all actual physical cache consumers. Allow a multi-node selected reader region only when its trusted prepared adapter supplies the exact paged input footprint/authority. Existing prepared-extension and RegionProjectedReadVTable are the natural seam to examine; do not authorize by a provider family whitelist.
fusion_proof_boundary.internal_fusion: Writer and reader in the same selected region need a real selected-artifact contract for internal write-before-read, exact dirty writers and effect preservation. Step order or permits_effects alone does not prove it. Do not simply allow equal step numbers or remove direct-edge/artifact checks.
fusion_proof_boundary.no_extra_dag_framework: Direct original edges remain sufficient for separate selected producer/reader regions. Avoid runtime graph traversal and a new general transitive dependency service; establish any expanded proof during cold binding/selection.

concrete_file_responsibilities.change: Remove redundant fixed logical rows from PagedAppend, or an equally small exact-input-derived representation; preserve exact rows validation in prepared child and target layout. Do not abandon the shared finite family.

Build paged math and direct edges, separate immutable whole snapshot from Invocation slots, add one step-transaction finish/abort, wire explicit fork/restore of the actual complete model state. Keep model-specific 24-layer layout here.
Retain count/pin/idle LRU role. Adjust byte admission at the actual physical shared-resource owner, not a duplicated per-session dense-state estimate; make any changed CLI byte scope explicit.
No new work required for the current proven singleton path. Extend only when an actual fused paged reader is selected and unsupported, preserving exact logical/physical/artifact proof.
No broad API expansion for first COW integration. Exclusive in-place mode and its failure semantics are a separate precise seam; preserve explicit reset/discard and actual-retirement gate.

One existing accepted-prefix failure injection through the transaction helper: old whole head unchanged, no partial layer publication, all original dirty owners recovered or still explicitly charged, then a subsequent fresh attempt can use reclaimed pages.

One same-user continuation without retained prefix to quantify COW bytes/preparation/replay changes; report correctness separately from throughput. Do not require a full platform/provider/model matrix before this first vertical slice.
performance_risks: Partial-tail COW is O(page_size) copy per decode step, not O(1); choose/measure page geometry rather than promising no regression.

Current append is capture_compatible=false; changing page/state-output bindings and taking pages invalidates recording. A full model may lose earlier CUDA capture benefits. First measure actual selected command/capture segments; do not hide this cost or claim memory-bound equivalence.
PagedAttention may select a different numerical/native route from the present fast RaggedAttention. Source-level availability does not establish end-to-end speed.
State buffers must come from bounded reusable pools; no per-layer native allocate or clone-for-write on every token. Captured pointer validity must follow actual bindings and original retirement.

Fixed-state snapshots cost 19,537,920 payload bytes for one current Qwen checkpoint before metadata/padding/workspace. Retained prefixes keep those real resources alive even though KV pages are shared.

Image projection and cross-device migration remain separate.
